chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us from his paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi —

that he asked Abu 'Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about fasting while residing at home (not travelling). He said: Three days every month — the Thursday before the first Friday, the Wednesday before the second Friday, and the Thursday before the third Friday. Al-Halabi said to him: Is this one day out of every ten days? He said: Yes.

And the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) has said: Fasting the month of Ramadan and three days every month removes anxieties from the chests. Fasting three days in every month equals fasting the whole year.
Verily God, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times its like.' [Quran 6:160]

key_terms.الحضر: Being resident at home, as opposed to travelling (al-safar), which has different fasting rulings
key_terms.بلابل الصدور: Anxieties, cares, and worries that reside in the chest/heart
key_terms.صيام الدهر: Fasting the whole year, a metaphorical equivalence in spiritual reward

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended fasting days each month according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) was asked about the recommended voluntary fasts for a resident (not travelling). He specified three days each month corresponding to the Thursday before each of the first, second, and third Fridays. He then confirmed that this pattern amounts to one day per ten days, and added the teaching of Imam 'Ali (AS) that fasting Ramadan plus these three monthly days removes heart-worries, and that three fasts per month equals a full year of fasting — justified by the Quranic principle of tenfold reward for good deeds. This teaching reflects the Shia jurisprudential tradition of recommended monthly fasts tied to specific days of the week, grounded in prophetic and Imamic precedent.
